summary: DONE holds for the cost the finding describes. Since 60633eff3 (#710), serializeProviderEventLogRecord swaps raw for a reference ({source, method, messageType, nativeId}) on every non-native record before JSON.stringify. The canonical log therefore no longer copies the SDK message on each fan-out event, whatever the provider or event type. Live logs confirm it: canonical files in ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider from Oct 14-15 have 0 lines with raw.payload, and raw is 7-16% of bytes, down from 43% typical and 87-95% in bursts. The large-workflow guard test exists. The auditor's line 'nothing is lost' is wrong for the packaged default 'lifecycle' mode. The native lifecycle filter drops most native messages that canonical lifecycle records point to, so on real threads 64-89% of canonical nativeIds point to native records that were never written, and that raw detail is now in neither log. This is a small diagnostics defect, not a performance gap.

evidence.note: serializeProviderEventLogRecord: for stream != native it uses withRawReference(record) before JSON.stringify. The over-cap walk and the replacer also run on the stripped value, so raw.payload is never visited.
withRawReference keeps source, method, messageType and nativeId = payload.uuid ?? payload.id. It applies no matter what the log mode is or whether the native log keeps that message.

The logger's serialize() calls the shared serializer. writeRecord (430-455) knows the mode but does not pass it on. The canonical delta-run record (providerEventLogRecords.ts:278-289) drops raw entirely.

publishRuntimeEvent writes the canonical log, then publishes to the PubSub. This is the only canonical write site. Runtime events are never serialized anywhere else; Diagnostics.ts:513-550 reads canonical lines without using raw.
Default mode is 'full' in development and 'lifecycle' when packaged. Native and canonical share one mode (185-197).

The native lifecycle filter keeps a method only if it matches init/start/started/end/complete/result/error and similar. It drops claude/system/status, claude/system/task_notification, claude/system/background_tasks_changed and claude/system/permission_denied, yet these back canonical lifecycle records (session.state.changed, task.completed, subagent.completed, task.started, tool.denied).

Recent canonical files: 0 raw.payload lines, raw is 6.6-15.8% of bytes. nativeId resolution against the matching .native.log: thread 803309ce 52 found / 433 missing, 76b51201 38/211, 08be3c64 54/85. The misses are almost all session.state.changed<-claude/system/status and task.completed<-claude/system/task_notification.

The Claude native record id is message.uuid, so canonical nativeId matches it in full mode. In full mode nothing dangles: thinking_tokens and ping, the only native records full mode drops, produce no canonical events (ClaudeAdapter.ts:4534).

Synthetic turn.started has payload {} and raw.payload {openedBy}, and no native record exists for it. The canonical log now loses whether a turn was opened by a wake signal or by a prompt. The claude.sdk.permission raw payloads (5280-5495) repeat what the canonical payload already holds, so dropping them loses nothing.

The Codex canonical eventId equals the native envelope id, so Codex records can be matched by eventId even though nativeId is usually missing (params have no uuid/id). This weakens the auditor's nativeId nit.
rawPayloadThreadId is still the only runtime reader of raw.payload. It is unaffected because stripping happens only in the log serializer.

Guard test: a 400-member workflow task.progress gives a canonical line under 2,048 bytes, raw becomes the reference, and the native stream keeps the message. It tests only the serializer, not the adapter-to-logger path, and has no lifecycle-mode case.

fixDefects: Not a performance defect, but a diagnostics regression in the shipped default. In 'lifecycle' mode, the default for packaged builds, withRawReference (providerEventLogRecords.ts:414-428) strips raw.payload from canonical lifecycle records whose native message the native lifecycle filter (providerEventLogRecords.ts:132-153) does not write: claude/system/status, task_notification, background_tasks_changed and permission_denied. That raw detail (for example permissionMode on status, output_file on task_notification) is therefore in neither log, and on live threads 64-89% of canonical nativeIds point to native records that do not exist. This contradicts the module comment (lines 13-15) and the auditor's 'nothing is lost'. Separately, synthetic raw payloads that never had a native record are now dropped in every mode. The only one carrying unique data is the turn.started {openedBy} at ClaudeAdapter.ts:3458-3462. Minor: the guard test is serializer-only and has no lifecycle case.
implementationSketch: Keep exactly one copy of each raw message in whichever log keeps it. (1) Pass the mode from EventNdjsonLogger.writeRecord through enqueueRecord and serialize into serializeProviderEventLogRecord(stream, record, mode). (2) In withRawReference, keep raw.payload when mode === 'lifecycle' and the native filter would drop raw.method. Reuse the existing policy: factor the name test out of isLifecycleProviderEventRecord into isLifecycleNativeName(name), and keep the payload when !isLifecycleNativeName(raw.method). Lifecycle records are low volume and task.progress is not lifecycle, so the burst cost does not come back; capping and redaction still apply. Do this only where the native message exists; for synthetic raw sources, also keep a raw.payload that is a small flat record (for example at most 4 own keys, all primitives, checked without stringifying), which saves {openedBy}. Alternatively, move openedBy into the turn.started payload. (3) Tests in providerEventLogRecords.test.ts: lifecycle + canonical task.completed with raw.method 'claude/system/task_notification' keeps payload; lifecycle + session.configured from 'claude/system/init' keeps only the reference; full mode always keeps only the reference; the existing 400-member guard still passes. Optionally add one EventNdjsonLogger test that writes a lifecycle-mode record and checks the file line.
decisionReason: This only changes what a local best-effort diagnostics log keeps at the lifecycle level. It touches no auth, E2EE, Hub protocol or hosted lifecycle rules.
correction: The auditor said every adapter that sets raw.payload also writes a native log, so nothing is lost. That holds only in 'full' mode. In the packaged default 'lifecycle' mode, the native filter drops most native messages that canonical lifecycle records point to (measured 64-89% missing on live threads), so that raw detail is now in neither log. Synthetic raw payloads such as turn.started {openedBy} never had a native copy. The auditor's nativeId nit is weaker than stated for Codex, because the Codex canonical eventId equals the native envelope id. The DONE classification for the performance cost stands.
